evidence: Searches of HHS OIG Whats New (July 16, 2026) and OIG Work Plan (items announced Aug 15 and 17, 2026) and GAO listings surface no formal HHS or congressional-committee audit report on the Deloitte Medicaid eligibility systems in the window; the only new items are the KFF Health News/NPR investigation (July 20-21, 2026) and IBTimes UK coverage (July 21, 2026), which are journalism, not a government audit.
disconfirming: Senate Finance Democrats sent inquiry letters to Deloitte and other contractors (Oct 10, 2025, per KFF Health News and CBS News) and state auditors (Michigan 2010, Kentucky 2016) issued earlier reports, but none is an HHS or congressional-committee audit report issued by 2026-08-15.
note: Criterion requires a public HHS or congressional-committee report confirming a formal audit with systemic IT-failure findings; a senators letter or press investigation does not satisfy it.

evidence: Nebius 6-K press release of March 11, 2026 (SEC EDGAR) states the pre-funded warrant was issued to Nvidia that day for aggregate gross proceeds of about $2.0 billion, and the Nebius Q1 2026 results 6-K (period ended March 31, 2026) reports $2,000.0 million in proceeds from the issuance of prefunded warrants within Q1 financing cash flows, i.e. the funds were received; Reuters and CNBC (March 11, 2026) covered the announcement.
disconfirming: No Nvidia or Nebius press release dated inside the forecast window (2026-07-21 to 2026-08-15) announces a new disbursement; the Nebius Q2 2026 shareholder letter (Aug 12, 2026, 6-K) discusses the ATM program and a $775M secured facility but does not restate the Nvidia disbursement.
note: Criterion as written has no start date and is satisfied by disclosures that predate the forecast issue date by four months; if the adjudicator requires an in-window announcement, nothing new was found and this becomes a MISS.

evidence: Al Jazeera (July 25, 2026) and bne IntelliNews (July 24, 2026) reported the government information council accusing IRIB of censoring Pezeshkian speech; Iran International (Aug 22, 2026) reported the IRGC chief publicly backing IRIB amid its clashes with Pezeshkian and Ghalibaf and stated the broadcaster still had not explained the omission, with no mention of the withheld remarks being aired or the dispute being settled.

evidence: FBI/EPA PSA (July 30, 2026) and CISA alert (July 30, 2026) describe a campaign against water-sector PLCs since July 27 in at least seven states; ABC News and CBS News (Aug 4-5, 2026) put it at 12 states with more than 30 Minnesota systems hit on July 26-27 and Clayton County GA disrupted in July, and CBS reported some utilities forced to manual mode but no impact on drinking water; no CISA or major-outlet report enumerates 15 or more utilities with a confirmed shutdown of operational control systems dated inside 2026-08-05 to 2026-08-15.
disconfirming: The campaign clearly exceeded 15 affected utilities in aggregate (30+ in Minnesota alone), with operator lockouts and manual operations documented by CISA and the FBI, so a lenient reading that ignores the window and treats loss of automated control as a shutdown could argue HIT.
note: The mass incidents are dated July 26-Aug 4, before the criterion window; in-window reporting was aggregate by state and ABC/CBS stated there were no widespread disruptions, so the 15-utility, in-window, shutdown-of-control threshold was not shown to be met.

evidence: The closest match is a TASS report (Aug 15, 2026) of a Russian MoD claim that Geran drones destroyed a military refueling point in Verbovka, Kharkiv Oblast, on the previous day (Aug 14); the ISW/Critical Threats assessment for Aug 15, 2026 records no Kharkiv City military-installation drone strike and lists Russian MoD drone claims for Chernihiv Oblast targets; Ukrainian officials reported only civilian-area strikes in Kharkiv around those dates.

evidence: No major-outlet transcript or video of a televised address by PM Andy Burnham between Aug 15 and Aug 18, 2026 criticizing Trump foreign policy was found; the only in-window Burnham broadcast item located is Bloomberg (Aug 18, 2026) reporting his remarks to broadcasters about messaging a Susie Wiles impersonator, with no foreign-policy criticism; Al Arabiya/Bloomberg (July 21, 2026) and Novara Media (July 22, 2026) show Burnham continuing Starmer policy of allowing US use of UK bases for Iran strikes.

evidence: Al Jazeera (Aug 7, 2026) reported Houthi drone and ballistic-missile strikes on Aug 6 against Saudi-led coalition and Yemeni government military sites in Hadramout and Marib, killing at least 30 soldiers, followed by at least 12 further Houthi missile attacks on Aug 7, plus a Houthi attack on Najran in southern Saudi Arabia that wounded 11 civilians per a Saudi official speaking to Reuters; Al Jazeera (Aug 9, 2026) reported a Houthi-claimed drone strike on the Aramco refinery in Jizan, which the Houthis framed as retaliation for Saudi drone incursions over Saada and Hajjah; Bloomberg (Aug 6, 2026) reported the same escalation.

evidence: Cisco published advisory cisco-sa-asaftd-vpn-dos-dzv4mQFF on Aug 11, 2026 stating PSIRT was aware of active exploitation of CVE-2026-20349, and BleepingComputer (Aug 11, 2026) and The Hacker News (Aug 11-12, 2026) reported the confirmed exploitation and the same-day CISA KEV addition with an Aug 14 federal deadline; follow-on write-ups from CyCognito, SOC Prime, OpenVPN and Ampcus Cyber appeared in the following days and Tech Insider (Aug 23, 2026) restated the active-exploitation finding.

evidence: Foreign Policy (Aug 13, 2026) reported water providers in at least seven states, possibly a dozen, were hit by cyberattacks confirmed by the FBI, EPA and CISA, with operators locked out of PLCs; TechCrunch (Aug 14, 2026) separately reported the FBI-confirmed campaign across roughly a dozen states including Minnesota, Arkansas, Georgia, New Jersey and Michigan; NPR (Aug 12, 2026) and Cybersecurity Dive (Aug 20, 2026) bracket the window with the same confirmed campaign.

evidence: CNN live coverage (Aug 15-16, 2026) and Alma Research (Aug 15, 2026) document the only in-window Iran-proxy action in the theatre: a Hezbollah attack on an IDF position on the Ali al-Taher ridge around Aug 14 that seriously wounded three soldiers, answered by Israeli strikes killing at least 11 in southern Lebanon and a senior Hezbollah commander; CNN (Aug 16) described a pause in US-Iran strikes, with Houthi activity confined to Yemen ports and Red Sea shipping.

evidence: Adobe patched Campaign Classic CVSS 10.0 flaws on Aug 1 (CVE-2026-48449, The Hacker News Aug 1, 2026) and again on Aug 11 (CVE-2026-48331, -48323, -48330; The Hacker News and Field Effect Aug 2026) and stated in each advisory that it was not aware of any exploitation in the wild; no disclosure from Adobe or any cybersecurity firm of exploitation between Aug 16 and Aug 23, let alone a breach affecting more than one million users, was found.
disconfirming: None found.
note: Threshold requires a disclosed exploitation-linked breach of over one million users; nothing approaching that exists in the record.

evidence: CENTCOM announced it completed a heavy wave of strikes on dozens of IRGC targets inside Iran by 10pm ET on July 29, 2026 after a five-night pause; Al Jazeera with Reuters (July 30, 2026) reported the strikes and Iranian reports of three civilians and three IRGC personnel killed, AP (Samy Magdy and Elena Becatoros, July 30, 2026, via Just Security) reported the same wave, and NPR, CNN and NBC News (July 29-30, 2026) carried it as well.
disconfirming: GlobalSecurity Day 179 update (Aug 25, 2026) says no US or Israeli strike inside Iran was confirmed after the president cancelled a threatened multi-day campaign late on Aug 1, so the qualifying strikes fall in the first days of the window and none later.
note: Two listed wires (Reuters via Al Jazeera co-byline, AP) reported a new US strike on Iranian territory dated July 29-30, inside July 27 to Aug 24.

evidence: In-window wire reporting documents the Greek toll rising past five: AP via PBS News (July 30, 2026) on two Crete firefighter deaths, Balkan Insight (Aug 3, 2026) citing five firefighters killed including two helicopter crew on Aug 2, and BBC (Aug 16, 2026) on two more deaths in the Salamis fires; the current Spanish events at issuance included the Almeria wildfire whose toll reached 14 by July 27 (Wikipedia citing La Razon and El Periodico; CNN/Reuters July 10, 2026) and a Manises death on July 25 (Mappr), so the combined Greece plus Spain toll exceeded 5 many times over.
disconfirming: The Spanish deaths were confirmed before July 31 and the Salamis deaths came from a fire that started Aug 16, so a strict reading that counts only deaths newly confirmed in-window from fires burning on July 31 gives Greece 5 (Crete 2, Peloponnese 1, helicopter crew 2) plus zero new Spanish deaths, exactly at rather than above the threshold.
note: Verdict depends on whether the Spanish July fires count as current events; on the plain reading of a combined Greece-Spain toll the threshold is clearly exceeded, on the strictest in-window-deaths-only reading it is met only by including the Aug 16 Salamis fatalities.

evidence: Senate roll call vote 230 (senate.gov, 119th Congress 2nd session) records the confirmation of Todd Blanche of Florida to be Attorney General at 4:17 AM on Aug 8, 2026, nomination PN1078; NPR (Aug 8, 2026) and The Washington Post (Aug 8, 2026) reported the 50-49 vote with Collins and Murkowski joining all Democrats in opposition.
disconfirming: None found.
note: Up-or-down floor vote occurred Aug 8, inside the Aug 4-21 window, and is recorded in the Senate roll-call record the criterion names.

evidence: The Washington DNR Wildfire Portal (dnr.wa.gov, read in late Aug 2026) lists all three Spokane Complex fires under past fires at 100 percent containment: Old Trails (3,621 acres) and Fairview (1,056 acres) with last updates of Aug 19, 2026, and Autumn Lane (5,603 acres) with a last update of Aug 21, 2026; Watch Duty citing NIFC and IQAir (Aug 25, 2026) also show all three at 100 percent, and InciWeb had them at 97 percent around Aug 13-14 (KHQ Aug 14, 2026).
disconfirming: Third-party trackers (AllFirefighter, Aug 17, 2026) still showed Old Trails at 98 and Autumn Lane at 97 percent on Aug 17, so full containment came in the final days of the window; the exact day Autumn Lane crossed to 100 percent is bounded by the DNR Aug 21 update rather than stated explicitly.
note: State fire authority (DNR) reported 100 percent containment with update dates of Aug 19 and Aug 21, inside the Aug 4-21 window and before the Aug 24 confirmation date.

evidence: The Oman Foreign Ministry site shows two Iran-Oman joint statements: one dated June 23, 2026 agreeing only to keep talking through a joint working group on future administration of Hormuz navigation, and one dated Aug 25, 2026 following foreign-minister consultations that Bloomberg (via Rigzone and Insurance Journal, Aug 26, 2026) describes as an interim framework for a temporary joint maritime corridor with technical talks continuing toward a permanent corridor; neither falls inside Aug 15-22 and neither specifies route coordinates or operational protocols.
disconfirming: Bloomberg (Aug 5, 2026) reported Iran saying agreement had been reached with Oman on a proposed shipping route and that a joint statement was in final drafting, which shows the process was active, but the statement itself only issued on Aug 25 and remained a framework for further talks.
note: The in-window requirement for a joint foreign-ministry statement confirming an established coordination agreement with coordinates and protocols was not met; the closest document is three days late and preliminary.

evidence: Wikipedia summary of the 2026 Colombia earthquake (updated Aug 25, 2026, citing USGS/ANSS and the Colombian Geological Survey) states the M7.4 mainshock of Aug 10 was followed by more than 100 aftershocks, the largest an mb 5.0 at 08:18 COT on Aug 10; CBS News/USGS (Aug 10, 2026) and Seismosoft (Aug 2026) likewise report the largest aftershock at M5.0 or M4.8; no news or agency report of an M6.0 or greater aftershock near us6000tjl2 between Aug 11 and Aug 22 was found.
disconfirming: None found; the USGS event page for us6000tjl2 notes aftershocks may follow but no M6+ event is reported in any source.
note: Could not query the USGS catalog API directly; verdict rests on catalog-derived summaries and absence of any M6+ aftershock reporting for a deep intraslab event whose largest recorded aftershock was M5.0.

evidence: Al Jazeera (Aug 18, 2026) reported the Electoral Commission of Zambia declaring Hakainde Hichilema president-elect early on Aug 18 with 2,965,326 votes, roughly 60-61 percent of valid votes, against 1,856,217 for Brian Mundubile; AP via The Washington Times (Aug 18, 2026) and APA News (Aug 18, 2026) carried the same declaration, and ECZ chair Mwangala Zaloumis was quoted declaring Hichilema president-elect this 18th day of August 2026.
disconfirming: The ECZ suspended counting for hours on Aug 14 amid violence and ballot-box theft claims, and the opposition alleged fraud (AP, Al Jazeera), but no runoff was called and no other winner declared.
note: ECZ formal declaration on Aug 18 falls inside the Aug 13-20 window with a first-round majority and no runoff.

evidence: CISA published its alert adding CVE-2025-62593 (Ray code injection) to the KEV catalog on Aug 17, 2026, with a BOD 26-04 federal remediation deadline of Aug 20; ComplianceHub (Aug 2026) and The Hacker News (Aug 17-18, 2026) both give the catalog date-added as Aug 17, 2026, consistent with the three-day deadline, not the Aug 18 value the criterion requires.
disconfirming: The entry does exist and was added one day earlier than forecast, so the substance of the claim (KEV listing around Aug 18) came true; only the exact date-added field fails.
note: Criterion demands a date-added value of exactly 2026-08-18; the record shows 2026-08-17, and the catalog JSON was not fetched directly to confirm the field.

evidence: Axios (Aug 5, 2026) reported the US, Iran and Oman were nearing an interim Hormuz reopening deal with a US announcement targeted for that Wednesday, but Al Jazeera (Aug 17, 2026) reported the US-Iran memorandum expiring with the strait still contested, the Washington Times/AP (Aug 26, 2026) reported the IRGC saying the strait stays closed until the US meets its terms, and the only concluded document was an Iran-Oman interim framework statement on Aug 25 (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Aug 26, 2026); no US and Iranian government confirmations of a concluded transit agreement between Aug 4 and Aug 21 appeared in any wire.
disconfirming: Trump cancelled a threatened bombing campaign around Aug 1 to allow diplomacy and talks continued through the window, but they produced no announced US-Iran agreement.
note: Both-government public confirmation via two wires is absent; the Aug 25 Iran-Oman statement is neither in-window nor a US-Iran agreement.

evidence: CISA added the Metabase SQL-injection vulnerability CVE-2026-72898 (CVSS 10.0, password-reset endpoint) to the KEV catalog on Aug 11, 2026 with an Aug 14 federal deadline, as reported by The Hacker News (Aug 2026), runZero (Aug 2026), GBHackers (Aug 2026) and TechTimes (Aug 12, 2026); Metabase had disclosed the zero-day attack on its Cloud service on Aug 6 and published fixes on Aug 10.
disconfirming: None found; the catalog JSON was not fetched directly but four independent security outlets give the same Aug 11 date-added.
note: Date-added of Aug 11 sits inside the Aug 9-23 window; the CVE number differs from the placeholder in some early coverage but it is the Metabase SQL-injection flaw the claim describes.

evidence: The US-acknowledged CENTCOM heavy wave of strikes on Iranian territory completed 10pm ET July 29, 2026 was reported by Reuters (co-bylined Al Jazeera report, July 30, 2026) and by AP (Samy Magdy and Elena Becatoros, July 30, 2026, cited by Just Security), with NPR (July 30, 2026) and CNN (July 29, 2026) quoting the CENTCOM acknowledgement; Al Jazeera characterized it as a resumption after a five-night pause.
disconfirming: GlobalSecurity Day 179 update (Aug 25, 2026) reports 26 consecutive nights without a confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iran after Aug 1, so the only in-window strikes are July 29-30; the Reuters and AP archives were not searched directly and their coverage is confirmed through co-bylines and citations rather than the archives themselves.
note: July 29-30 strikes sit inside the July 28 to Aug 26 window and were publicly acknowledged by CENTCOM; a BBC report was not separately verified but two of the three named outlets suffice.

evidence: Searches for Al Jazeera and BBC World coverage of a new political scandal involving a US federal official between Aug 11 and Aug 18, 2026 surfaced only continuing coverage of the Blanche confirmation fallout (CNN and The Hill, Aug 16, 2026) and general scandal roundups from earlier in the year (The Week May 1, 2026; The Fulcrum March 25, 2026); no in-window Al Jazeera or BBC World report on a newly emerged federal-official scandal was identified.
disconfirming: The criterion is broad (any federal official, any scandal) and both outlets publish heavily on Washington, so a qualifying pair of reports could exist without surfacing in keyword searches; nothing located confirms it either way.
note: Could not verify or rule out; adjudicator with archive access to Al Jazeera and BBC World for Aug 11-18 should decide, since the search record here is inconclusive rather than negative.

evidence: No report from both a Russian-aligned and a Ukrainian source of a Shahed-type strike on a civilian infrastructure site in Donetsk with structural damage between Aug 21 and Aug 24, 2026 was found; ISW/Critical Threats (Aug 21-24, 2026) records Russian drone packages hitting Donetsk Oblast among other regions on Aug 20-21 per Ukrainian officials, and Reuters photographs (Aug 16, 2026) show Ukrainian drone damage in occupied Donetsk City, but neither is a dual-source, in-window, Shahed-on-civilian-site report.
disconfirming: The resolution criterion is written as a negation (the KEV catalog does not carry such an entry and no two sources corroborate) while the failure condition describes the positive event; read literally the negation is satisfied by the absence found here, which would make this a HIT rather than a MISS.
note: Inverted criterion: the adjudicator must decide whether absence of a corroborated Shahed strike scores as a HIT under the resolution text or a MISS under the claim; the record supports absence either way.

evidence: AP (via The Washington Times, Aug 20, 2026) reported a Russian missile and drone barrage on Kyiv and Kyiv region killing at least 16 with heavily damaged residential buildings; Reuters photographers and reporting carried by Al Jazeera (Aug 16, 2026) documented the Aug 16 missile strike on a Kyiv book market, and AP (via NPR/PBS, Aug 16, 2026) reported six wounded in that attack; CNN and RFE/RL (Aug 5, 2026) reported the Aug 5 attack on Kyiv Oblast killing 17.
disconfirming: None found.
note: Multiple in-window Kyiv strikes with damage and casualties were reported by at least two of the named wires.

evidence: For the night of Aug 19-20, the Ukrainian Air Force (relayed by ISW/Critical Threats Aug 20, 2026) reported a single strike package on Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast comprising ballistic and quasi-ballistic missiles, ground- and air-launched cruise missiles, ship-launched cruise missiles, Banderol loitering munitions and Shahed-type strike drones, while the Russian Defense Ministry (TASS and Sputnik via GlobalSecurity, Aug 20, 2026) described the same overnight massive strike on Kyiv and the Kyiv region as using precision land-, air- and sea-launched weapons plus long-range UAVs; AP (via The Washington Times, Aug 20) reported at least 16 killed.
disconfirming: The Russian MoD statement describes weapon categories by launch platform rather than naming missile types, so a strict reader might want explicit RU-side naming of four types; ISW also noted the Ukrainian Air Force stopped publishing ballistic-missile counts on Aug 11, so numbers per type are unavailable.
note: Both sides describe one Aug 19-20 wave on Kyiv with at least four distinct weapon classes (ballistic, cruise, loitering munition, strike drone); the corroboration is by category rather than by named system.

evidence: Al Jazeera with AFP and Reuters (Aug 16, 2026) reported that the Romanian Ministry of National Defence announced on Sunday Aug 16 that a Spanish F-18 on a NATO air-policing mission shot down a drone that had breached Romanian airspace from the direction of Moldova, with NATO military headquarters spokesman Martin ODonnell (surname spelled with an apostrophe in the original) saying the drone appears to be Russian and Romanian Defence Minister Radu Miruta hailing the mission; ISW/Critical Threats (Aug 20, 2026) also records a Romanian F-16 destroying a naval drone near the Neptune Deep platform on Aug 20.
disconfirming: the Romanian statement itself described the drone by its entry point rather than explicitly naming Russia, and the Aug 20 naval-drone incident was outside territorial waters with origin unspecified, so the Russian attribution for the Aug 16 shootdown rests on the NATO spokesmans characterization.
note: A NATO member government (Romania) confirmed the downing inside its territory on Aug 16 and NATO itself attributed the drone to Russia, satisfying the criterion within the Aug 11-24 window.

evidence: The CISA KEV catalog vendor listing for SonicWall shows the two SMA1000 entries, CVE-2026-15409 (SSRF) and CVE-2026-15410 (code injection), with a date-added of 2026-07-14 (CISA KEV page; SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer, July 15, 2026); the Aug 10, 2026 change flagged them as used in ransomware campaigns (BleepingComputer Aug 10, 2026; Tech Insider Aug 2026) but did not create a new entry or alter the date-added, and no other SonicWall SMA1000 CVE was added between Aug 10 and Aug 24.
disconfirming: The Aug 10 ransomware-use update generated fresh coverage that could be mistaken for a new listing; it is a metadata update on entries dated July 14.
note: Criterion turns on a dateAdded value inside Aug 10-24; the only SMA1000 entries carry July 14.

evidence: Aug 23, 2026 was a Sunday with no NYSE session and therefore no settlement price; the surrounding closes were all well below 7,800: CNBC (Aug 21, 2026) reported the S&P 500 closing at 7,674.37 on Friday Aug 21, Yahoo Finance shows a close of 7,677.28 on Aug 25 (up 24.42, implying about 7,652.86 on Aug 24), and Advisor Perspectives (Aug 21, 2026) put the index 1.6 percent below its Aug 13 record close.
disconfirming: The failure condition as written (closes below 7,800 on Aug 23) is also literally unmet because there was no close, so a purist could argue for AMBIGUOUS; every adjacent trading day resolves the same way.
note: No trading on the specified date; the last close before and the first close after were both roughly 125-150 points under the threshold.

evidence: CISA added CVE-2025-62593, the Ray code-injection flaw, to the KEV catalog on Aug 17, 2026 (CISA alert Aug 17; ComplianceHub Aug 2026), based on evidence of active exploitation, and The Hacker News (Aug 17-18, 2026) documents a public proof-of-concept exploit incorporated by the RondoDox botnet and active ShadowRay 2.0 campaigns against unpatched Ray instances.
disconfirming: None found; the catalog JSON was not fetched directly, but the CISA alert page itself is dated Aug 17 and BOD 26-04 due date of Aug 20 implies the same date-added.
note: One qualifying entry with date-added inside Aug 17-20 suffices; the Ray entry has both a public exploit and confirmed in-the-wild use.

evidence: ISW/Critical Threats (Aug 22, 2026) relays Ukrainian Railways CEO Oleksandr Pertsovsky reporting a Russian strike on a railway enterprise in Kyiv City on the night of Aug 21-22 that killed one employee, and its Aug 21 assessment lists Kyiv Oblast among the regions where Ukrainian officials reported Russian drone impacts from the 135-drone overnight package; both are Ukrainian-side (UA) confirmations inside Aug 21-24.
disconfirming: The Aug 21-22 Kyiv railway strike is not explicitly typed as a drone strike in the ISW summary, although the overnight package that night was drone-only per the Ukrainian Air Force; no Russian-side confirmation was sought since one hostile-side report suffices.
note: Ukrainian official reporting of a Kyiv strike during a drone-only Russian package satisfies the one-hostile-side criterion; the drone attribution is inferred from the package composition.

evidence: Reporting on exploitation of CVE-2025-62593 clusters around the Aug 17, 2026 KEV addition, with The Hacker News (Aug 17-18, 2026) and CyberUpdates365 (Aug 2026) citing the March 2026 BitSight RondoDox findings and the Oligo ShadowRay 2.0 campaign; no source located confirms a cyberattack exploiting the flaw that occurred or was first reported between Aug 21 and Aug 24, 2026.
disconfirming: Exploitation campaigns against Ray were described as ongoing, so attacks in the window are plausible, but no dated confirmation from two independent sources exists for Aug 21-24.
note: Absence of in-window confirmations scores MISS; earlier campaign reporting does not satisfy a window-specific two-source criterion.

evidence: The French wildfire-monitoring association Feux de Foret (feuxdeforet.fr, read Aug 26, 2026) lists 654 validated fires in France in the prior 30 days and shows the Luglon/Morcenx-la-Nouvelle fire in the Landes (started Aug 13, roughly 170 ha) still tracked as active with updates through late August, alongside the Saumos, Biscarrosse and Bellegarde-en-Diois fires; its Aug 19 and Aug 21 articles cover the Gros Bessillon extinction and the FireWatch detection platform, and Wikipedia describes 2026 as the worst French fire season since 1949 with 115,000 ha burned.
disconfirming: The criterions hostile-side list (IL, PS, AXIS, WEST) fits a conflict template poorly; the only sensible reading is that any Western source counts, and the evidence here is the live tracker of a French monitoring site rather than a wire article dated to a specific day in Aug 21-24.
note: Wildfires were burning and tracked in France throughout Aug 21-24 during a record season; the adjudicator should confirm the WEST label covers French domestic sources.

evidence: Middle East Eye live blog (Aug 23, 2026) citing the Palestinian news agency WAFA reported an Israeli drone strike north of Khan Younis that wounded six Palestinians when two missiles hit a tent near the Albanian mosque, with four more wounded in a separate attack north of the city the same day; Al Jazeera (Aug 25, 2026) reported a further drone strike in Khan Younis al-Mawasi area on Aug 25.
disconfirming: None found; the Israeli side did not comment on the Aug 23 strike, but the criterion needs only one hostile-side (PS via WAFA) report.
note: Palestinian-side confirmation of a Khan Younis drone strike on Aug 23 sits inside the Aug 21-24 window.

evidence: the Threema post-incident statement (Aug 14, 2026) and coverage by BleepingComputer, Security Affairs (Aug 16, 2026) and Cybersecurity News date the large-scale DDoS attacks to Tuesday evening Aug 11 through Wednesday morning Aug 12, 2026, with four hours of complete unavailability, after which Threema deployed upstream DDoS filtering; no source reports a further DDoS disruption of Threema between Aug 21 and Aug 24.
disconfirming: Some secondary write-ups (Rescana) misdate the incident to Aug 13-14, but all versions place it before the Aug 21 window opens.
note: The forecast was issued Aug 17, after the only reported Threema DDoS disruption of the month; nothing recurred in-window.

evidence: TASS (Aug 23, 2026) reported Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin stating that air defenses shot down six drones flying toward Moscow with emergency crews working at the debris sites, and TASS (Aug 22, 2026) reported the Sobyanin tally of more than 2,500 drones sent toward the Moscow region since Aug 15 with 493 destroyed on the approach to the city; ABC News (Aug 26, 2026) reported Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow resuming after a pause for the CIA directors visit.
disconfirming: The Aug 23 RU-side report describes drones downed on approach with debris falling rather than a confirmed impact on a target in Moscow, so a strict reading of drone strike could treat it as an attempted attack; the largest Moscow raids (Aug 16 and Aug 18) fall before the window.
note: Russian officials confirmed a drone attack on Moscow on Aug 23; whether interception-with-debris equals a strike is the interpretive question.

evidence: ISW/Critical Threats (Aug 22 and Aug 24, 2026) records geolocated Russian Geran drone strikes on locomotives near Mykolaivka, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, and Ukrainian reports of drone damage to infrastructure in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on the night of Aug 23-24, and the Zelensky account of the Aug 21 double-tap drone strike on a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre that killed 16; none of these is in Dnipro city itself and no Dnipro-city drone strike report dated Aug 21-24 was located.
disconfirming: Dnipro city is struck frequently and a local report may exist that keyword searches missed; the oblast-level confirmations are unambiguous but the criterion names Dnipro.
note: Resolves HIT if Dnipro is read as the oblast (Ukrainian officials confirmed drone strikes there Aug 21-24) and unverified if read as the city.

evidence: Middle East Eye (Aug 23, 2026) and Reuters via US News (Aug 23, 2026) reported an Israeli raid on the Askar refugee camp east of Nablus in which a 14-year-old was shot dead, plus raids on Beita, Tal and Beit Dajan and the continuing settler siege of Qusra; none of the Nablus-area incidents between Aug 21 and Aug 24 involved a drone strike, and no IL, PS or Axis-side report of a drone strike in Nablus was found.
disconfirming: Israeli forces do use drones in West Bank operations and WAFA reporting is granular, so a small drone incident could have escaped keyword searches, but the well-covered Aug 23 Nablus events were shootings and raids.
note: Absence of any hostile-side drone-strike report for Nablus in the window scores MISS.

evidence: ISW/Critical Threats (Aug 21 and Aug 23, 2026) relays Ukrainian officials, including the Sumy Oblast Military Administration Telegram channel, reporting Russian drone strikes that damaged commercial, residential, agricultural and electrical infrastructure in Sumy Oblast during the 135-drone package of Aug 20-21 and the 127-drone package of Aug 22-23.
disconfirming: The confirmations are at oblast level; a Sumy-city-specific drone strike report dated Aug 21-24 was not separately located, so a strict city reading would leave this unverified.
note: Ukrainian (UA) official reporting confirms drone strikes in Sumy region on two nights in the window; adjudicator should decide whether the criterion means the city or the oblast.
